newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks move higher after brief pause.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks move higher after brief pause.

text.p: U.S. blue chips and technology stocks climbed on Thursday, eyeing further gains in the bond market after data which showed a 2.2 percent annualized rise in the second quarter gross domestic product.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which made a slight pause in early trading, was up 26 points at 8281.
The Nasdaq composite rose four points to 1592.
Bonds led the way, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond gaining 16/32 to yield 6.29 percent.

"The GDP data was very good," Alfred Kugel, Stein Roe & Farnham senior investment strategist, said. "Concerns we had several months ago about the economy overheating and interest rates racheting up have all but vanished."

But stocks backed off slightly after the Conference Board reported the U.S. help wanted index read 88.0 in June compared to 81.0 in May. The Conference Board said the U.S. labor market was expanding "about as fast as it possibly can."
The Chicago Purchasing Managers Index read 60.6 in July versus a 61.5 reading in June.
On Friday, the market will face July employment data.
